That changes it: `python deploy.py` invokes the Python interpreter, which reads the script file (needs read permission). The execute bit is irrelevant. Permission denied means the script is hitting it on something it opens—a file, directory, or resource it tries to access during execution.

To narrow it down: run the script with more verbose output or strace/similar to see what path fails. Or check the full error message—it usually names the file or resource that was denied.

grade.note: Reply agrees the execute bit is irrelevant and correctly attributes the error to file/resource access, matching ground truth.
